title: [Planned future feature] Parallelization of the main loop
body:
The main loop used to calculate distances between atoms is 100% parallelizable, this can be improved In several ways, like:

- With a divide-and-conquer algorithm reducing the order from an N^2 to an N log N paradigm.
- With multithreaded loop. 

Almost 90% of the execution time is spent in this loop, so every optimization matters.

title: [Planned future feature] Structure factor

title: [Planned future feature] Velocity Correlation Functions
body:
Velocity Correlation Function is fundamental is one of the most used time dependant correlation functions, and is used to study diffusion as well as phase transitions.

This function could benefit the study of amorphous and liquid materials as well as the trajectory files.

title: CFGrote's JOSS Review
body:
Hi @Isurwars.
First off, great work and very useful. Please find my comments and notes while working on the JOSS Review checklist https://github.com/openjournals/joss-reviews/issues/2976.

#### Installation
* There is no `configure` step involved which means if I had non-standard settings on my computer, `make` might fail to locate the compiler and/or libraries. Also, installing into a target directory is not supported (no install target).
* You could explain why the user should run `make clean` **after** building.
* The binary produced by the `make all` step has the windows-typical '.exe' extension. This is a bit unusual for linux/mac.
#### Functionality
* `make tests` produces no errors, however it remains unclear if that just means the program ends or if it actually passed unittest and/or regression tests. Probably related to #5. 
* Running the individual test with `./bin/correlation.exe test/test_1/aPd.cell`
  returns "File not found". aPd.cell is in test_3, test run is ok. 
* Plotting the resulting PDF from test_3 gives the following figure:
![Figure_1](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/15476807/108195232-ca784c00-7117-11eb-9684-64e887df2ac6.png).
 You might consider putting this or a similar graph into the README and instruct the user to try and reproduce this result as a confirmation the code works as it should.
* Performance: You claim that your code can handle up to 25000 atoms. I could not find a demonstration of such a system. Is it in test_6? If so, you should clearly mention it.

#### Documentation
* I find the output not properly documented (neither in the paper nor in the README): Describe the content of each file, describe what each column contains and specify the units. At a minimum, this information should go into the header of each .csv file. As a perspective, I recommend storing the results in a self-documenting format, e.g. hdf5.
* You should document the command line options in the README.
* No automated tests, see comment above. Adding tests that compare the code's output to reference data will make the validity of your code more accessible.
* No community guidelines (probably related to #6)

#### Paper
* Summary:
    * You state that the code is ready for mac while the README says mac not supported due to compiler issues.
    * A non-expert reader will be overwhelmed by the technical and field specific jargon. I advise to write something like: "Our code calculates various correlation functions from atomic positions".
    * Your claimed limit of 25000 atoms is not a lot (e.g. in biomolecules). What causes this limit? Does it depend on hardware/software on the user's system?
* Statement of need: 
    * name and cite other packages (earlier, in statement of need). Please check the exhaustive list of software in the Computational Physics Communications archive http://cpc.cs.qub.ac.uk/, the IUCr's software list https://www.iucr.org/resources/other-directories/software for similar software. What is particular about your software that makes it stand out from other packages?
    * clearly name target audience
* Benchmarks, validation:
    * define test_x as being included in the software package. a table with
      references would be helpful. 
    * Is test_6 really a challenge? it completes on my laptop in a few
      seconds. What are the limiting factors? memory/cpu? What exactly do you mean 
      by "... benchmark  memory and CPU performance ...". The sentence on line 91-93 mentions test_6 and test_4, it is not clear which one you refer to here.
* Conclusion:
    * You mention HPC here but HTC (high throughput computing) earlier. What exactly do you mean here? Does your code support parallelization using e.g. MPI or similar frameworks? Suppose I want to run a large system that does not fit into memory, can your code deal with it? How do you address parallel IO?
    * How will it be extended, which features are missing?

title: Add contributing guidelines
body:
Currently there is no clear guidance for contributors to learn about the projects. I usually consider it very helpful to have clear expectations spelled out in a dedicated contributing guideline. There are plenty of resources around for writing contributing guidelines, have a look at your favorite projects or maybe look at this collection here (https://github.com/nayafia/contributing-template) for inspiration.

If you don't want to add a full contributing guideline yet, consider at least to add a section to your README describing the recommended way to
1. submit patches
2. report bugs
3. ask for help

GitHub offers a community profile at every repository that can guide you through the process of refining your projects presentation to the open source community (see https://github.com/Isurwars/Correlation/community).

title: Testing and continuous integration
body:
The testing is currently only limited to performing a few sample calculations, but the results are in no way checked for correctness. While this testing strategy will catch fatal errors that lead to aborted runs it will not cover the correctness of the produced results. 

Another point is that the testing of the command line interface is not covering all options sufficiently, only a single command line option is actually present in the tests.

I think, it is highly advisable to have a unit testing or at least meaningful end-to-end testing for the command line interface in place to ensure that the functionality in this package keeps working.

Additionally, I recommend to have a look into continuous integration (CI). For a quick start on CI setup I recommend to have a look into GitHub Actions, it offers a Windows Server runner which comes with an easy-to-use MSYS2 toolchain (see https://github.com/marketplace/actions/setup-msys2).

title: Joss Review
body:
I'm looking into your Correlation project as part of your submission to JOSS (see https://github.com/openjournals/joss-reviews/issues/2976).

Some things I stumbled upon first looking at this project

- [x] ``clang++`` seems to be supported just fine, but is currently explicitly marked as not supported
- [x] the getting started section mentioned deployment, but there is no section on deployment
- [ ] the license file linked in the README is not present in the repository, the link should point to ``LICENSE`` rather than ``LICENSE.md``
- [x] binary files are checked into git (``bin/Correlation.exe``), I would recommend to remove them as they cannot be meaningfully tracked by a version control system
- [ ] a number of typos in the README makes it rather hard to read, especially if they present in program names (*e.g.* LAAMPS should be LAMMPS)
- [x] the test example in the README is not present in the repository at `test/test_1/aPd.cell` but `test/test_3/aPd.cell`

I will open separate issues as well for more concrete issues as well.

title: Cryptic error for -w option
body:
The `-w` arguments seems to behave strangely, at f23d1383a96510a9085e418c5c401f7235286f0b I get for any input

```
Starting program: /home/awvwgk/projects/src/joss/Correlation/_build_debug/Correlation -w 0.02 test/test_2/Graphene.car
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::logic_error'
  what():  basic_string::_M_construct null not valid

Program received signal SIGABRT, Aborted.
0x00007ffff7ac5615 in raise () from /usr/lib/libc.so.6
```

With the patch c5a37aadbb7814b81ea4cc315ea71670a27d06ca the `-w` argument is always in error

```
Starting program: /home/awvwgk/projects/src/joss/Correlation/_build_debug/Correlation -w 0.02 test/test_2/Graphene.car
Invalid input: '[Inferior 1 (process 29177) exited with code 01]
```

Checking the state of `optarg` in the `case 'w':` reveals that it is null. Note that this does not happen if `--bin_width` is used to specify the option.

title: Uncaught exception for invalid command line arguments
body:
Running this project with invalid command line arguments like a string passed to the ``-a`` option results in an unhandled exception:

    Starting program: /home/awvwgk/projects/src/joss/Correlation/_build_debug/Correlation test/test_1/xSi.car -a str
    terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::invalid_argument'
      what():  stof

    Program received signal SIGABRT, Aborted.
    0x00007ffff7ac5615 in raise () from /usr/lib/libc.so.6

Preferrably the exception is caught by the program and converted to a meaningful error message for the user to understand the problem with the input.
